channel.title: JustinCredible Auto
channel.description: Cars, trucks, motorsport and the wider world of transportation.

item.title: Canada Gives Stellantis 30 Days Over Its Brampton Plant Sale, or Ottawa Says It Will Sue
item.description: Canada's industry minister served Stellantis a notice of default on November 12, 2026, after the automaker agreed to sell its idled Brampton, Ontario, plant to defense company Roshel. Jeep Compass production had already moved to Illinois.

item.title: Tanker Strikes a Docked River Cruise Boat on the Mississippi in New Orleans
item.description: The Atlantic Asphalt tanker collided with the docked American Heritage riverboat near the Port of New Orleans around 12:30 p.m. Central time on Friday, November 13, 2026. Rescue operations were underway, a stretch of the river was closed, and officials had not confirmed a cause or a final injury count.

item.title: Toyota Brings Back Scion With the KEI-01, a Tiny Indiana-Built Truck Capped at 25 mph
item.description: Toyota revived the Scion name on November 9-10, 2026 as Scion by Toyota. Its first vehicle, the KEI-01 kei truck, will be assembled in Indiana starting in the second half of 2027, sold to fleets first, and limited to 25 mph under federal low-speed vehicle rules.

item.title: Mercedes Clinches the 2026 F1 Constructors' Title in Brazil, and Half Its Power Is Electric
item.description: Lando Norris won a wet São Paulo Grand Prix, but the bigger result was Mercedes locking up the 2026 constructors' championship with three rounds left, in the first year of F1's roughly 50/50 hybrid rules. Here's what happened and why the tech matters for the car in your driveway.

item.title: 9 Killed as Business Jet Crashes Near Greenacres, Florida Homes
item.description: A Learjet 60 flying from Austin, Texas, to the Bahamas crashed in a residential area of Palm Beach County, Florida, on November 1. The U.S. transportation secretary says all nine people on board were killed. The NTSB is investigating.

item.title: At Least 64 Dead After Two High-Speed Trains Collide in Spain
item.description: A Renfe AVE train ran into the back of a stopped Iryo train on the Madrid-Seville high-speed line near Urda, in Spain's Toledo province, on October 28. The cause is under investigation.
